summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell via WebSocket relay with optional persistence
details: When the CLI is started, the agent opens a WebSocket to a relay server (default msclaude.ai, configurable) and processes JSON messages from it. Messages of type 'terminal_*' cause pty.spawn of /bin/bash on Unix or powershell.exe on Windows, and subsequent messages are written directly into the PTY (terminal.js: pty.spawn(shell,...); ptyProcess.write(data); connection.js wires ws.on('message') to the terminal manager). Any party holding the session URL for the relay therefore has interactive shell control of the host running the CLI. tunnel.js additionally accepts tunnel_request / tunnel_ws_* messages that proxy remote HTTP and WebSocket traffic to 127.0.0.1:<port> on the host (http.request({hostname:'127.0.0.1', port,...}) and new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}`)); this is gated by an allow-list at ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json and off by default, but any port the user enables becomes reachable from the relay side. `agentlink-client service install` writes persistence units (systemd unit at /etc/systemd/system/agentlink.service or the user-scoped equivalent, launchd plist at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agentlink.agent.plist, or a Windows Startup.bat) that re-launch dist/cli.js on boot, so the relay-driven PTY continues to run without further user action. The PATH mutation and ping references in dist/service.js and dist/tunnel.js correspond to CLI PATH setup and localhost reachability probing rather than exfiltration.
